title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol: we judge faith/obedience necessary to eternal life by fixed decree — yet as special gift prepared in predestination, produced by special operation, foreseen as medium not motive
pass_a_gloss: We on the contrary, although we judge the condition of faith and of obedience (if we speak of adults) plainly necessary unto obtaining everlasting life from the fixed decree of God, yet we acknowledge that this faith and obedience was not foreseen in this or that singular person as springing from his free choice excited by common grace, and dragging after itself the benefit of election; but as a special gift prepared from eternity for this and that singular person in the decree of predestination, and to be produced from the human will by a certain special operation depending from the same decree, and thence foreseen from eternity in all the elect, not as a motive by which they themselves obtain their election, but as a medium by which preceding they will obtain the kingdom of the heavens unto which they were elected.
pass_b_english: We take the other side. For adults we judge faith and obedience plainly necessary to everlasting life by God's fixed decree. Yet we deny that this faith and obedience was foreseen in this or that person as something springing from free choice stirred by common grace, and then dragging election's benefit after it. We hold instead that it was a special gift, prepared from eternity for each elect person in the predestination decree. It is to be produced from the human will by a special operation that depends on that decree. From eternity, then, it was foreseen in all the elect — not as the motive by which they win their election, but as the preceding medium by which they reach the kingdom of heaven to which they were elect.
source_text: Nos e contra, quamvis fidei et obedientiae conditionem (si de adultis loquamur) ad vitam aeternam consequendam, ex Dei fixo decreto plane necessariam judicemus, tamen agnoscimus hanc fidem et obedientiam non praevisam fuisse in hac aut illa singulari persona, tanquam ex libero ejus arbitrio per gratiam communem excitato enascentem, et electionis beneficium post se trahentem; sed tanquam speciale donum fuisse huic et illi singulari personae in decreto praedestinationis ab aeterno praeparatum, et ex humana voluntate speciali quadam operatione ab eodem decreto dependente producendam, et inde ab aeterno praevisam in omnibus electis, non tanquam motivum quo ipsi consequantur suam electionem, sed tanquam medium quo praecedente consequentur regnum caelorum ad quod fuerunt electi.
